title: Activator-to-Binder Ratio–Driven Microstructural and Interfacial Performance Optimization of Metakaolin-Based Geopolymer Coatings
content: Metakaolin-based geopolymer coatings (GCs) represent an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional protective coatings, but their effectiveness is highly influenced by formulation parameters. In this study, the effect of activator/binder (a/b) ratio on the microstructural development, interfacial adhesion, and mechanical performance of metakaolin-based geopolymers was systematically investigated. Three ratios (0.3, 0.4, 0.5) were evaluated for pull-off adhesion, pencil hardness, 3D profilometry, FTIR, XRD, and digital microscopy. The 0.3 ratio provided weak geopolymerization, high roughness (Sa = 42.8 µm), and low hardness, which were beyond the valid range. Both 0.4 and 0.5 yielded coherent coatings, but with distinct performance: 0.4 maximized adhesion due to moderate roughness (Sa = 27.1 µm) and optimal thickness; 0.5 maximized scratch hardness due to a smoother surface (Sa = 9.1 µm). Increasing the a/b ratio increased porosity via excess water evaporation and reduced cross‑linking density. Digital microscopy confirmed no early‑age drying damage. The processing window for metakaolin‑based GCs is a/b = 0.4–0.5, within which adhesion (0.4) or hardness (0.5) can be prioritized, providing a rational formulation framework for tunable geopolymer coatings.
